state.name: West Virginia
state.agency: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Section
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May during spring raccoon and squirrel denning and groundhog emergence, summer for bat maternity colonies in attics and peak copperhead activity, and late September through November as rodents, squirrels, and bats seek winter shelter in homes across the mountains and river valleys
state.climate_factor: West Virginia's mountain winters push rodents, squirrels, and bats into attics and wall voids hard, while warm humid summers in the Ohio River and Kanawha valleys drive heavy raccoon, skunk, and groundhog activity; elevation changes the calendar by weeks between the Eastern Panhandle and the high Allegheny counties
state.permit_note: West Virginia requires a Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA) license, issued by the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources under W. Va. Code §20-2-50a and 58 CSR 41, for commercial nuisance wildlife work; a WDCA may control only the species listed in 58 CSR 41 §7.1.g, may never control the species listed in §7.1.i, and under §8.1 must euthanize captured wildlife humanely or liberate it at the site of capture — off-site release requires the prior approval of the district wildlife biologist

Barbour County.region: north-central West Virginia in the Tygart Valley
natural_features: Alum Cave and the Middle Fork River corridor
Barbour County.habitat_type: river-valley towns under steep wooded ridges, with farms and camps along the Tygart and Middle Fork
Barbour County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the Tygart River bottoms and Philippi's older blocks, gray squirrels fill the oak ridges above the valley towns, and woodchucks burrow the farm edges around Belington and Junior
Barbour County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the county but may be controlled only with prior approval from the WVDNR district biologist and a Natural Resources Police officer, not as routine work

Berkeley County.region: the Eastern Panhandle along I-81, bordering Maryland and Virginia
Berkeley County.nearest_metro: Washington, DC (about 75 miles southeast) and Hagerstown, MD (about 20 miles north)
natural_features: Back Creek and the Potomac River border
Berkeley County.habitat_type: fast-growing I-81 subdivisions and Martinsburg's older urban core, backed by orchard land, karst limestone, and wooded ridges in the west
Berkeley County.regional_wildlife: woodchucks burrow under sheds and decks across the orchard-edge subdivisions from Inwood to Hedgesville, skunks work the new lawns along I-81, Norway rats hold Martinsburg's oldest blocks, and bats turn up in both 1800s downtown homes and brand-new attics in the exurban growth ring
Berkeley County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live in the county's western ridges and creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the county's limestone caves are bat habitat where listed species are referral-only, never a service

Boone County.region: southwestern West Virginia coal country along the Coal River
natural_features: Coal River and Little Coal River
steep reclaimed mine land and ridge forests
Fork Creek Wildlife Management Area (in neighboring Lincoln, serving the same ridge country)
Boone County.habitat_type: narrow Coal River valley towns tucked against steep wooded ridges, with homes and camps strung along the hollows
Boone County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Coal River bottoms and the valley towns nightly, snakes — mostly harmless rat snakes and garter snakes, with copperheads on the rocky cuts — turn up around stone walls and woodpiles, and bats roost in older hollow homes and outbuildings
Boone County.absent_or_rare: black bears and white-tailed deer are common on the reclaimed ridges but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and beavers flooding hollow roads are likewise approval-gated, never routine services

Braxton County.region: the geographic center of West Virginia, on the Elk River
Braxton County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 60 miles southwest) and Clarksburg (about 45 miles north)
natural_features: Bulltown and the West Fork corridor
Braxton County.habitat_type: lake and river country of small valley towns, camps, and farmhouses under heavy forest cover
Braxton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the Elk River and lake shoreline camps, bats colonize older Sutton and Gassaway homes and seasonal lake houses, and woodchucks and skunks handle the farm-edge digging around Flatwoods
Braxton County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are plentiful around the lakes and river bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval rather than as routine removal work

Brooke County.region: the Northern Panhandle on the Ohio River, bordering Ohio and Pennsylvania
Brooke County.nearest_metro: Pittsburgh, PA (about 35 miles east) and Steubenville, OH (across the river)
Brooke County.habitat_type: Ohio River mill towns and older suburbs under wooded bluffs, with farmland on the plateau above
Brooke County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in the older riverfront blocks of Wellsburg and Follansbee, raccoons and bats work the bluff-side homes above the river, and skunks and opossums fill the suburban yards in between
Brooke County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the riverfront are federally protected — deterrence only, never a removal service

Cabell County.region: western West Virginia on the Ohio River at the Kentucky and Ohio tri-state
Cabell County.nearest_metro: Huntington is itself the tri-state metro center
natural_features: Ohio River and Guyandotte River confluence
Ritter Park and the Fourpole Creek corridor
Beech Fork State Park (southern county line)
Cabell County.habitat_type: the Huntington urban core and older suburbs, with river-bottom towns and wooded hill neighborhoods throughout
Cabell County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats anchor calls in Huntington's oldest neighborhoods and commercial blocks, raccoons and gray squirrels work the hill and park-side streets, pigeons and starlings roost on downtown commercial buildings, and bats colonize older homes from the Southside to Barboursville
Cabell County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the Guyandotte and Beech Fork but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the riverfront are deterrence-only under federal protection

Calhoun County.region: central West Virginia on the Little Kanawha River
natural_features: steep forested ridges and oil-and-gas country
Cedar Creek State Park (just over the Gilmer line)
Calhoun County.habitat_type: one of the state's most rural counties — small river towns, farm bottoms, and homes scattered through deep forest
Calhoun County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Little Kanawha bottoms, gray and fox squirrels fill the ridge oak woods, bats roost in the county's older farmhouses and churches, and harmless rat snakes are routine around barns and woodpiles
Calhoun County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are all common but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes on the rocky ridgetops are never a removal promise — safety and identification only

Clay County.region: central West Virginia on the Elk River
natural_features: Buffalo Creek and the county's steep hollow country
Clay County.habitat_type: deeply rural Elk River valley and hollow communities under near-total forest cover
Clay County.regional_wildlife: raccoons commute from the Elk River bottoms into the town of Clay and the hollow homes, bats settle the older farmhouses, and woodchucks and skunks work the cleared bottoms and garden plots
Clay County.absent_or_rare: black bears and white-tailed deer are abundant in the surrounding forest but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and beaver work on the creeks is approval-gated as well

Doddridge County.region: north-central West Virginia on Middle Island Creek
Doddridge County.nearest_metro: Clarksburg (about 30 miles east) and Parkersburg (about 40 miles west)
Doddridge County.habitat_type: small rail-trail towns and farm country on rolling wooded ridges
Doddridge County.regional_wildlife: woodchucks burrow the farm and garden edges around West Union, raccoons work the Middle Island Creek bottoms, and bats and squirrels share the county's older farmhouses
Doddridge County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live throughout the creek country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval rather than as routine services

Fayette County.region: south-central West Virginia at the New River Gorge
Fayette County.nearest_metro: Beckley (about 25 miles south) and Charleston (about 55 miles northwest)
natural_features: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
New River and Gauley River confluence
Babcock State Park and Hawks Nest State Park
Fayette County.habitat_type: gorge-rim towns, rafting and vacation properties, and older coal and railroad towns along the rivers
Fayette County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the gorge country's steady pair — raccoons in Fayetteville and Oak Hill attics and vacation rentals, bats in older homes and cabins near the rim — while copperheads keep to the rocky gorge slopes and stone walls, and skunks work the town yards at dusk
Fayette County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and river otters live in the gorge but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the Allegheny woodrat in the gorge's rock outcrops is a never-control species — referral only, never a service

Gilmer County.region: central West Virginia on the Little Kanawha River
Gilmer County.nearest_metro: Weston (about 25 miles northeast) and Charleston (about 75 miles southwest)
Gilmer County.habitat_type: a small college town in a river bottom, surrounded by farm clearings and deep forest
Gilmer County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share Glenville's older homes — bats in the summer attics, raccoons in the chimneys — woodchucks work the Cedar Creek farm country, and squirrels fill the ridge woods pressing every clearing
Gilmer County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are common in the forest and creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Grant County.region: the Potomac Highlands on the South Branch Potomac River
Grant County.nearest_metro: Winchester, VA (about 55 miles east) and Cumberland, MD (about 50 miles north)
natural_features: North Fork Mountain and the Monongahela National Forest edge
Grant County.habitat_type: river-valley farm towns under high ridges, with poultry country, camps, and second homes along the South Branch
Grant County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the South Branch bottoms and Petersburg's older streets, woodchucks and skunks dig the farm and garden edges, timber rattlesnakes keep to the rocky North Fork Mountain slopes, and bats roost in valley homes and riverside camps
Grant County.absent_or_rare: black bears and white-tailed deer are plentiful on the ridges but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the timber rattlesnake — the state reptile — is safety and identification work only, never a lethal service

Greenbrier County.region: southeastern West Virginia in the Greenbrier Valley, bordering Virginia
Greenbrier County.nearest_metro: Beckley (about 45 miles west) and Roanoke, VA (about 70 miles southeast)
natural_features: Greenbrier State Forest and the karst cave country
Greenbrier County.habitat_type: a broad limestone farm valley with historic towns, cave and karst country, and forested mountain edges
Greenbrier County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels work Lewisburg's historic streets and the valley farms, moles tunnel the limestone valley's lawns and pastures, woodchucks burrow the farm edges, and bats roost in older valley homes — with the county's caves reserved for the protected species that are never ours to disturb
Greenbrier County.absent_or_rare: the Virginia big-eared bat and Indiana bat in the county's caves are federally endangered and never-control species — referral to WVDNR and USFWS only — and black bears, deer, and beavers may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval

Hampshire County.region: the Potomac Highlands on the South Branch Potomac, the state's oldest county
Hampshire County.nearest_metro: Winchester, VA (about 35 miles east) and Cumberland, MD (about 30 miles northwest)
natural_features: South Branch Potomac River and The Trough
Capon River and Cacapon River country
Short Mountain and Nathaniel Mountain WMA
Hampshire County.habitat_type: river-valley farm towns, orchard country, and ridge-and-hollow homes and camps between the South Branch and the Cacapon
Hampshire County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the South Branch bottoms and Romney's older streets, woodchucks burrow the orchard and farm edges around Capon Bridge, skunks dig the valley lawns, and copperheads favor the rocky ridge slopes and stone walls above the rivers
Hampshire County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the valley and ridge country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes on the rocky ridges are identification and safety work only

Hancock County.region: the northernmost Northern Panhandle on the Ohio River and Pennsylvania line
Hancock County.nearest_metro: Pittsburgh, PA (about 35 miles southeast) and Steubenville, OH (about 15 miles south)
natural_features: steep wooded bluffs above the river towns
Hancock County.habitat_type: Ohio River industrial and residential towns under wooded bluffs, with suburban growth around Weirton
Hancock County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold the older riverfront and industrial blocks of Weirton and New Cumberland, raccoons and squirrels work the bluff-side neighborhoods, and bats return to the county's older homes every summer
Hancock County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the river are federally protected — deterrence only

Hardy County.region: the Potomac Highlands on the South Fork of the South Branch Potomac
Hardy County.nearest_metro: Winchester, VA (about 50 miles east) and Harrisonburg, VA (about 45 miles southeast)
natural_features: South Fork Potomac River and Moorefield Valley
Lost River and the trough country of the west
Warden Lake and Trout Pond recreation country
Hardy County.habitat_type: a wide poultry-and-farm river valley between high ridges, with camps and homes along the South Fork and Lost River
Hardy County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the South Fork bottoms and Moorefield's older streets, woodchucks and skunks dig the poultry-farm and garden edges, bats roost in valley homes and river camps, and copperheads and timber rattlesnakes keep to the rocky ridge slopes
Hardy County.absent_or_rare: black bears and white-tailed deer are common on the ridges but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the timber rattlesnake, the state reptile, is safety and identification work only — never a lethal service

Harrison County.region: north-central West Virginia on the West Fork River
Harrison County.nearest_metro: Clarksburg-Bridgeport is the regional center; Morgantown is about 35 miles north
natural_features: rolling gas-country hills and river bottoms
Harrison County.habitat_type: Clarksburg's older urban neighborhoods and Bridgeport's fast suburbs, with small coal and rail towns and farm country between
Harrison County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Clarksburg's oldest blocks, raccoons and squirrels work the canopy neighborhoods of Clarksburg, Bridgeport, and Salem, bats colonize the county's deep stock of early-1900s homes, and woodchucks and skunks handle the suburban-edge digging in Shinnston and beyond
Harrison County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the West Fork bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and black bears in the county's wooded east are likewise approval-gated

Jackson County.region: western West Virginia on the Ohio River and Mill Creek
Jackson County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 35 miles southeast) and Parkersburg (about 35 miles north)
natural_features: rolling farm and forest country throughout
Jackson County.habitat_type: Ohio River town at Ravenswood, the Ripley farm-and-suburb center, and rural homes across rolling farm country
Jackson County.regional_wildlife: woodchucks and moles work the farm and lawn country around Ripley, raccoons and bats fill the older homes of Ripley and Ravenswood, and skunks and opossums cover the rural yards in between
Jackson County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live along the river and creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Jefferson County.region: the Eastern Panhandle at the Potomac and Shenandoah confluence, the state's easternmost county
Jefferson County.nearest_metro: Washington, DC (about 60 miles southeast) and Winchester, VA (about 25 miles southwest)
natural_features: Potomac River and Shenandoah River confluence at Harpers Ferry
Blue Ridge foothills and the Appalachian Trail corridor
limestone karst and cave country under the valley floor
Jefferson County.habitat_type: historic towns, horse-and-farm country, and fast DC-exurban subdivisions over limestone karst
Jefferson County.regional_wildlife: woodchucks burrow the horse-farm and subdivision edges from Charles Town to Shepherdstown, raccoons and squirrels work the historic towns' old housing, bats roost in 1800s homes and the county's karst-edge buildings, and black rat snakes are routine around barns and stone walls
Jefferson County.absent_or_rare: the Indiana bat and Virginia big-eared bat in the county's caves are federally endangered never-control species — referral only — and white-tailed deer and beavers may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval

Kanawha County.region: central West Virginia on the Kanawha River — the state's most populous county
Kanawha County.nearest_metro: Charleston is the state capital and metro center
natural_features: Kanawha River and Elk River confluence at Charleston
Coonskin Park and Kanawha State Forest
steep wooded hills framing every valley neighborhood
Kanawha County.habitat_type: the Charleston urban core and river suburbs, chemical-valley towns downstream, and hollow communities up every creek
Kanawha County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats anchor the oldest Charleston and valley-town blocks, raccoons and squirrels work the hill neighborhoods that rise straight from the streets, pigeons and starlings roost on downtown and plant-area commercial buildings, and bats colonize older homes from Charleston to St. Albans
Kanawha County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live in Kanawha State Forest and the creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the riverfront are deterrence-only under federal protection

Lewis County.region: north-central West Virginia on the West Fork River
natural_features: West Fork River and Stonewall Jackson Lake
Lewis County.habitat_type: the Weston valley town, lake communities, and farm-and-forest country throughout
Lewis County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share Weston's older homes, woodchucks and skunks work the farm edges, and lake-area camps around Stonewall Jackson Lake open each spring to overwinter raccoon and bat sign
Lewis County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live around the lakes and river bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Lincoln County.region: southwestern West Virginia in the Guyandotte and Mud River country
Lincoln County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 30 miles northeast) and Huntington (about 25 miles northwest)
natural_features: Mud River and its lake at Eleanor (neighboring Putnam)
Lincoln County.habitat_type: rural river-valley and hollow communities with farm clearings under steep forest
Lincoln County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Mud and Guyandotte bottoms nightly, woodchucks burrow the cleared farm edges, and bats and squirrels share the older hollow homes
Lincoln County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the river country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval rather than as routine services

Logan County.region: southwestern West Virginia coal country on the Guyandotte River
natural_features: steep reclaimed mine land and ridge forest
Logan County.habitat_type: coal-valley towns and hollow communities tucked under steep wooded and reclaimed ridges
Logan County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Guyandotte bottoms and every hollow community, bats roost in the older valley homes, and copperheads favor the rocky mine-bench and stone-wall country above the towns
Logan County.absent_or_rare: black bears are genuinely common on the reclaimed ridges — Chief Logan's bears are famous — but bears, deer, and beavers may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, never as routine services

McDowell County.region: the southernmost West Virginia coalfields, bordering Virginia
McDowell County.nearest_metro: Bluefield (about 35 miles east) and Beckley (about 55 miles north)
natural_features: steep coal-country ridges and hollow country throughout
McDowell County.habitat_type: historic coal towns in narrow valleys, hollow communities, and some of the most rugged forest in the state
McDowell County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Tug Fork bottoms and every coal town, bats colonize the deep stock of coal-era homes in Welch and War, and snakes — rat snakes around the houses, copperheads on the rocky slopes — are a routine summer call
McDowell County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are abundant in the forest but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes in the high rocky country are safety and identification work only

Marion County.region: north-central West Virginia on the Tygart and Monongahela rivers
Marion County.nearest_metro: Fairmont is a regional center; Morgantown is about 20 miles northeast
natural_features: Tygart River and Monongahela River confluence at Fairmont
Marion County.habitat_type: Fairmont's older urban neighborhoods, Mannington's small-town core, and suburbs and farms across rolling hills
Marion County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats persist in Fairmont's oldest blocks, raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the canopy neighborhoods on both river hills, and woodchucks and skunks cover the farm and suburban edges around Mannington and Pleasant Valley
Marion County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live along the river bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine removal work

Marshall County.region: the Northern Panhandle on the Ohio River, below Wheeling
natural_features: Fish Creek and Grave Creek country
Marshall County.habitat_type: Ohio River towns under the bluffs, with suburbs and farms on the plateau above
Marshall County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats hold the older riverfront blocks of Moundsville and Benwood, raccoons and bats work the bluff-side and older housing, and skunks, opossums, and woodchucks fill the plateau suburbs and farms
Marshall County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the riverfront are federally protected — deterrence only

Mason County.region: western West Virginia at the Ohio and Kanawha confluence
Mason County.nearest_metro: Gallipolis, OH (across the river) and Huntington (about 40 miles south)
natural_features: Ohio River and Kanawha River confluence at Point Pleasant
broad river bottoms and farm country
Mason County.habitat_type: historic Point Pleasant at the confluence, river towns up both shores, and farm country across the bottoms and hills
Mason County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work Point Pleasant's historic homes, woodchucks and moles handle the farm and lawn country, and skunks and opossums cover the river-town yards from New Haven to Mason
Mason County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, bald eagles along the rivers, and beavers live in the bottoms and at McClintic but are managed by WVDNR — beaver work may be done only with prior WVDNR approval, and eagles are federally protected

Mercer County.region: southern West Virginia on the Virginia line, along I-77
natural_features: Bluestone River and Bluestone State Park country (northern county)
high ridge-and-valley country along East River Mountain
Mercer County.habitat_type: Princeton's suburbs and Bluefield's historic hillside neighborhoods, with farm valleys and mountain towns between
Mercer County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the older homes of Princeton and Bluefield, woodchucks and moles handle the farm-valley lawns and gardens, and skunks and opossums cover the ridge-town yards from Athens to Bramwell
Mercer County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the Bluestone and mountain country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Mineral County.region: the Potomac Highlands on the North Branch Potomac, bordering Maryland
natural_features: Knobly Mountain and the Ridgeley bluffs
Mineral County.habitat_type: river and rail towns along the North Branch, with farm valleys and forested ridges behind
Mineral County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the older homes of Keyser, Piedmont, and Ridgeley, Norway rats hold the oldest riverfront and rail blocks, and woodchucks and skunks cover the farm-valley edges
Mineral County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the ridge and river country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Mingo County.region: southwestern West Virginia coal country on the Tug Fork, bordering Kentucky
Mingo County.nearest_metro: Pikeville, KY (about 30 miles south) and Logan (about 30 miles north)
natural_features: Hatfield-McCoy trail country in the ridges
Mingo County.habitat_type: Tug Fork valley towns and hollow communities under steep forested and reclaimed ridges
Mingo County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Tug Fork bottoms and every hollow, bats roost in the coal-era homes of Williamson and Matewan, and copperheads favor the rocky slopes and stone walls above the towns
Mingo County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are common in the ridge country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, never as routine removal work

Monongalia County.region: north-central West Virginia on the Monongahela River, bordering Pennsylvania
Monongalia County.nearest_metro: Morgantown is a metro center; Pittsburgh, PA is about 75 miles north
Monongalia County.habitat_type: Morgantown's university neighborhoods and fast suburbs, river towns, and forested ridge country in the east
Monongalia County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats work Morgantown's canopy neighborhoods and student rentals, Norway rats hold the oldest downtown and riverfront blocks, and woodchucks and skunks cover the suburban ring from Westover to Cheat Lake
Monongalia County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the Coopers Rock and Cheat country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Monroe County.region: southeastern West Virginia in the Greenbrier and New River country, bordering Virginia
Monroe County.nearest_metro: Lewisburg (about 25 miles north) and Bluefield (about 45 miles southwest)
natural_features: Peters Mountain and the karst valley country
Monroe County.habitat_type: one of the state's most pastoral counties — farm valleys, small towns, and karst cave country under Peters Mountain
Monroe County.regional_wildlife: woodchucks and moles work the farm valleys around Union and Peterstown, raccoons and bats share the older farmhouses, skunks dig the valley lawns, and snakes — rat snakes at the barns, copperheads on Peters Mountain's rocky slopes — round out the summer calls
Monroe County.absent_or_rare: the caves of the karst country hold federally listed bats that are never-control species — referral to WVDNR and USFWS only — and black bears, deer, and beavers may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval

Morgan County.region: the Eastern Panhandle between the Potomac River and Cacapon Mountain
Morgan County.nearest_metro: Winchester, VA (about 35 miles southeast) and Hagerstown, MD (about 30 miles northeast)
natural_features: Cacapon Mountain and Sleepy Creek country
the warm springs at Berkeley Springs State Park
Morgan County.habitat_type: the historic spa town of Berkeley Springs, river and mountain cabins, and rural homes and second homes throughout
Morgan County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the cabin country's pair — both move into Berkeley Springs-area homes and second homes that sit quiet in the week — woodchucks and skunks work the cleared lots, and copperheads favor Cacapon Mountain's rocky slopes and stone walls
Morgan County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the mountain and river country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes on the rocky ridges are safety and identification work only

Nicholas County.region: central West Virginia on the Gauley and Meadow rivers
Nicholas County.nearest_metro: Beckley (about 40 miles south) and Charleston (about 65 miles west)
natural_features: Carnifex Ferry and the Meadow River country
Nicholas County.habitat_type: Summersville's growing lake-and-highway town, Richwood's mountain valley, and farm-and-forest country throughout
Nicholas County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share the older homes of Summersville and Richwood and the lake houses around Summersville Lake, woodchucks and skunks work the farm and yard edges, and squirrels fill the oak woods pressing every town
Nicholas County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the river and forest country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Ohio County.region: the Northern Panhandle on the Ohio River, bordering Ohio and Pennsylvania
Ohio County.nearest_metro: Wheeling is the regional center; Pittsburgh, PA is about 55 miles east
Ohio County.habitat_type: Wheeling's dense historic neighborhoods and brick core, island housing, and hill suburbs above the river
Ohio County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats anchor Wheeling's oldest riverfront, island, and commercial blocks, raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the canopy hill neighborhoods, pigeons and starlings roost on downtown commercial buildings, and skunks and opossums fill the suburban yards
Ohio County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along Wheeling Creek but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese on the riverfront and island are federally protected — deterrence only, never removal

Pendleton County.region: the Potomac Highlands — the state's highest, most mountainous rural county
natural_features: Spruce Knob, the highest point in West Virginia
South Branch Potomac headwaters and cave country including Hellhole
Pendleton County.habitat_type: high mountain farm valleys, tiny valley towns, and camps under the state's tallest ridges
Pendleton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share the valley farmhouses around Franklin, woodchucks and skunks work the farm edges, and timber rattlesnakes keep to the rocky high slopes around Seneca Rocks and Spruce Knob — identification and safety country, not removal country
Pendleton County.absent_or_rare: Hellhole cave's Indiana bats and Virginia big-eared bats are federally endangered never-control species — referral only — and black bears, deer, and beavers may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval

Pleasants County.region: western West Virginia on the Ohio River, between Parkersburg and New Martinsville
natural_features: Ohio River shoreline and Middle Island
Pleasants County.habitat_type: the small river city of St. Marys, Belmont, and rural homes across bluff and farm country
Pleasants County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work St. Marys' older homes, skunks and opossums cover the river-town yards, and woodchucks dig the farm edges around Belmont
Pleasants County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the river and creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and bald eagles on the river are federally protected

Pocahontas County.region: the Potomac Highlands — birthplace of rivers, the state's most mountainous eastern county

Pocahontas County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats are the high-country pair — raccoons in Marlinton and Durbin attics, bats in mountain homes and ski-area properties — woodchucks work the Greenbrier farm valleys, and timber rattlesnakes keep to the rocky Cheat Mountain slopes
Pocahontas County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are abundant in the national forest but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the Allegheny woodrat and northern flying squirrel in the high country are never-control species — referral only

Preston County.region: north-central West Virginia high country, bordering Maryland and Pennsylvania

Preston County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the older homes of Kingwood, Terra Alta, and Rowlesburg, woodchucks and skunks cover the plateau farm country, and porcupine sign in the high woods is prose wildlife, not a service — our calls stay with the house-and-yard animals
Preston County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the Cheat gorge and creek country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Putnam County.region: western West Virginia on the Kanawha River, between Charleston and Huntington
Putnam County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 25 miles east) and Huntington (about 25 miles west)

wooded ridges framing the valley suburbs
Putnam County.habitat_type: Teays Valley's fast suburbs, Winfield's river town, and farm-and-ridge country in the north
Putnam County.regional_wildlife: squirrels and raccoons work the maturing Teays Valley canopy in Hurricane and beyond, woodchucks and skunks dig the subdivision and farm edges, moles tunnel the valley lawns, and bats and rats hold the older Winfield and Buffalo river stock
Putnam County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the Kanawha and creek bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Raleigh County.region: southern West Virginia on the New River, along I-77 and I-64

Raleigh County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the gorge and creek country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine removal work

Randolph County.region: the Potomac Highlands on the Tygart Valley River

Randolph County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, squirrels, and bats work Elkins' older neighborhoods and the valley towns, woodchucks and skunks cover the farm country, and timber rattlesnakes keep to Cheat Mountain's rocky slopes — safety and identification country
Randolph County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are abundant in the national forest but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the northern flying squirrel and Allegheny woodrat are never-control species — referral only

Ritchie County.region: northwestern West Virginia in the Hughes River and North Bend country
natural_features: Hughes River and North Bend State Park
rolling oil-and-gas farm and forest country

Roane County.region: central West Virginia in the Spring Creek and Pocatalico country
natural_features: Spring Creek and Charles Fork Lake

Roane County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live along the creeks but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Summers County.region: southern West Virginia on the New River, bordering Virginia
natural_features: Bluestone Lake and Bluestone State Park
Summers County.habitat_type: Hinton's historic rail-town terraces and rural New River and Greenbrier valley communities
Summers County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work Hinton's terraced historic homes, skunks and opossums cover the river-town yards, and copperheads favor the rocky New River slopes and stone walls above the bottoms
Summers County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live throughout the river country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes on the high rocky ground are safety and identification work only

Taylor County.region: north-central West Virginia on the Tygart Valley River
Taylor County.nearest_metro: Clarksburg (about 20 miles southwest) and Fairmont (about 20 miles north)
natural_features: Tygart Valley River and Tygart Lake
Taylor County.habitat_type: Grafton's historic rail town in the Tygart valley, Flemington's small borough, and farm country throughout
Taylor County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share Grafton's deep stock of older homes, woodchucks and skunks work the farm edges, and squirrels fill the valley oaks pressing every roof in town
Taylor County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live along the Tygart and its creeks but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Tucker County.region: the Potomac Highlands — high Allegheny country of Canaan Valley and Blackwater Falls

Tucker County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are abundant in the high country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and the northern flying squirrel and Allegheny woodrat are never-control species — referral only

Tyler County.region: western West Virginia on the Ohio River, in the Sistersville oil country
Tyler County.nearest_metro: New Martinsville (about 15 miles north) and Parkersburg (about 45 miles south)

Tyler County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work the oil-era homes of Sistersville and Middlebourne, skunks and opossums cover the river and creek bottoms, and woodchucks dig the farm edges on the ridges
Tyler County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the river and Middle Island Creek but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and bald eagles on the river are federally protected

Upshur County.region: central West Virginia on the Buckhannon River

Upshur County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers live in the foothill forest and river bottoms but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine work

Wayne County.region: westernmost West Virginia on the Ohio and Big Sandy rivers, bordering Kentucky and Ohio
Wayne County.nearest_metro: Huntington (the county's northern edge reaches the Huntington metro)
natural_features: Ohio River and Big Sandy River (western borders)
Wayne County.habitat_type: tri-state river towns at Kenova and Ceredo, the Wayne valley town, and rural ridge-and-hollow country in the south

Wayne County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live around Beech Fork and East Lynn but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Webster County.region: central West Virginia in the Elk and Gauley headwaters — among the most rural counties in the East

Webster County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are abundant in the mountain forest but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and timber rattlesnakes on the rocky high ground are safety and identification work only

Wetzel County.region: western West Virginia on the Ohio River, below the Northern Panhandle
Wetzel County.nearest_metro: New Martinsville is the local center; Parkersburg is about 55 miles south

wooded bluffs and oil-and-gas ridge country
Wetzel County.habitat_type: New Martinsville's river city, small creek towns like Pine Grove and Hundred, and ridge farm country
Wetzel County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats work New Martinsville's older homes, Norway rats hold the oldest riverfront blocks, and skunks, opossums, and squirrels cover the creek towns and ridge farms
Wetzel County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along the river and creeks but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and bald eagles on the river are federally protected

Wirt County.region: western West Virginia on the Little Kanawha River — the state's least populous county
Wirt County.habitat_type: the tiny river town of Elizabeth and deeply rural farm-and-forest country
Wirt County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and bats share Elizabeth's older homes, opossums and skunks work the river bottoms, and woodchucks dig the scattered farm clearings
Wirt County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer, black bears, and beavers live along the Little Kanawha but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, not as routine services

Wood County.region: western West Virginia at the Ohio and Little Kanawha confluence
natural_features: Ohio River and Little Kanawha River confluence
Mountwood Park and the Hughes River country (eastern county)
Wood County.habitat_type: Parkersburg's urban core and older suburbs, Vienna and Williamstown's river suburbs, and farm-and-forest country in the east
Wood County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats anchor Parkersburg's oldest neighborhoods and commercial blocks, raccoons, squirrels, and bats work the canopy suburbs of Vienna and Parkersburg, pigeons and starlings roost on downtown commercial buildings, and skunks and woodchucks cover Williamstown and the rural east
Wood County.absent_or_rare: white-tailed deer and beavers live along both rivers but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, and Canada geese and bald eagles on the river and Blennerhassett Island are federally protected — deterrence and referral only

Wyoming County.region: southern West Virginia coal country on the Guyandotte River
Wyoming County.habitat_type: coal valley towns at Pineville, Mullens, and Oceana, and hollow communities under steep ridges

Wyoming County.absent_or_rare: black bears, white-tailed deer, and beavers are common in the ridge country but may be controlled only with prior WVDNR approval, never as routine removal work
